value.rationale: Strict ternary betweenness is a standard relational structure, but its binary static and adaptive shattering capacities differ even for the smallest nontrivial four-point paths. The threshold at four, persistence at five, and an exact component-profile formula for an unbounded number of unknown component-path arrangements give a mathematically motivated and reusable baseline for finite-structure identification. It is stronger than merely enumerating a fixed small family because all large disjoint path-forest concept classes with prescribed supports of size at most five are classified; no unrestricted-tree theorem is claimed.
